comments.body:
RE-TYPED bug -> story and left OPEN and UNCLAIMED for a dedicated implementer. Not abandoned: the plan in the description is the current, four-times-reviewed design and is the right starting point.

WHY. This began as a follow-up split out of silvern-dewy-damselfly's plan review — 'make the closed-without-signature state detectable by a later reader'. Four plan reviews grew it well past bug-follow-up size, and each round was legitimate discovery rather than wording:

R1 BLOCK — a single boolean cannot express the multi-way discriminator the ACs demand, and the plan never said how 'a signature was expected' is computed or threaded (it is NOT verified_result, which is None for a --force close even though a signature WAS expected).
R2 BLOCK — the enum omitted the DISPOSITION close, a genuinely distinct expectation that _completion_precheck already produces (close_precheck.py:441-446) and that would otherwise misread as a verified completion; and it omitted the config-unreadable fail-open, where recording gate_off would launder a FAULT into a policy choice. Also: AC2 requires reading from reduced state, so the reducer fold and ticket_state schema had to join the edit set.
R3 BLOCK (new scope, which is why this stops here) — two structural findings the earlier rounds had not reached. gate_enabled (gates.py:79-87) returns a bare bool that is False for BOTH gate-off and config-unreadable, so it COLLAPSES the two before _completion_precheck can observe the difference: the enum cannot be produced without changing that function's signature, a new edit site the plan does not own. And idea->closed never enters _completion_precheck at all (close_ticket guards the call with current_status != 'idea'), so not_applicable has no named computation site.

WHERE IT STANDS. The current description carries: an 8-value completion_expectation enum recorded on the close STATUS event in the same locked write as the close (no extra lock — which is the whole point, since an audit comment or second event would append through the very lock whose timeout causes the failure being recorded); a derivation table combining the durable expectation with the durable attestation; and the close_class precedent for event-write + fold-at-both-*->closed-edges + reduced-state schema.

WHAT THE NEXT IMPLEMENTER MUST RESOLVE FIRST (the R3 findings):
1. gate_enabled must distinguish gate-off from config-unreadable, or the expectation must be computed somewhere that can see the difference. Its current fail-open bool is the blocker.
2. Name an owner for not_applicable, since idea->closed bypasses _completion_precheck entirely.
3. Add ACs exercising gate_unreadable and disposition — R3 correctly noted both carry distinct semantics with no criterion asserting them.

NOT BLOCKING ANYTHING SHIPPED. silvern-dewy-damselfly (change 1673) makes the loss machine-readable to the caller that suffered it across library, CLI and MCP, and is independent of this. This ticket is only about an unrelated LATER reader.

Related: defiant-orthoclase-buck (055d-f176-8fcb-4ffe) touches the same STATUS event with a much smaller change and should be sequenced with this, not merged into it.

compiled_state.description:
Split from silvern-dewy-damselfly (f4cf-60b2-41c0-4843) during its plan review.

## Problem

After a close whose completion-signature append failed, a later reader cannot reliably tell
that ticket apart from one closed with the gate off. Damselfly makes the loss machine-readable
in the RETURNED PAYLOAD of the call that suffered it, but that payload is ephemeral and never
persisted. An agent that was not the caller, or the same agent in a later session, has no
durable discriminator.

## Premise verified in code — PARTIALLY true, narrower than first written

The original draft claimed all three states are indistinguishable. That overstates it:
verification found one existing discriminator, **the `COMPLETION_VERDICT` PASS sidecar**
(`llm/completion_sidecar.py:202` `latest_pass_record`), emitted on EVERY completion PASS at
`_commands/close_precheck.py:577-580`, before signing and before the close commits:

| state | `attestations["completion-verifier"]` | PASS sidecar |
|---|---|---|
| (a) closed, attestation valid | present | present |
| (b) closed, signature failed to persist | absent | **present** |
| (c) closed, gate OFF | absent | absent |

(b) is therefore already distinguishable via `audit/read.py:113-123`. Three caveats keep that
from being a real answer: the sidecar is **reducer-ignored** (`completion_sidecar.py:10-16` —
not in `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`, so it never reaches compiled state and `rebar show` cannot see it,
only the audit surface); its emit is **best-effort**, dropped with only a stderr warning
(`close_precheck.py:349-355`); and `prune()` deletes it after `RETAIN_PER_TICKET = 10`.

**(c) has no discriminator at all, and that is the sharper bug.** The gate's on/off state at
close time is nowhere in the store — it is read from config and discarded
(`_commands/close_precheck.py:410-416`; key `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close`
at `_config_schema.py:159`, default False). So "closed with no attestation" collapses these
into ONE indistinguishable state:

* gate genuinely off (`close_precheck.py:416`)
* `--force` close (`close_precheck.py:417`)
* config unreadable → `gate_enabled` **fails OPEN** (`_commands/gates.py:79-87`)
* `source == "local"` unattested close (`close_precheck.py:585-586`)
* `certifiable is False` withholding (`close_precheck.py:589-600`)
* a dropped PASS sidecar

Worse, `txn.transition_core` **accepts `force_close_reason` and never uses it**
(`_commands/txn.py:198` — one occurrence, silently discarded though `transition_close.py:474`
passes it), so a force close leaves no durable reason. Tracked separately as
defiant-orthoclase-buck. The close STATUS event records only `status`, `current_status`,
`parent_status_uuid` and present-only `close_class` (`txn.py:277-296`;
`docs/event-schema.md:47`).

## Direction

Record, on the close STATUS event, WHY a completion signature was or was not expected — in the
same locked write that already commits the close (`txn.transition_core`), so NO additional lock
acquisition is needed. That is the whole point: an audit comment or a second event would append
through the same `event_append` -> `write_lock` path whose 60s timeout causes the failure being
recorded, and would be missing exactly when it matters.

**It must be an ENUM, not a boolean.** A single bool cannot separate the states the ACs demand.
The field is `completion_expectation`, total over the close path:

| value | meaning at close time |
|---|---|
| `required` | the gate ran and a completion signature was expected |
| `disposition` | a bug closed `duplicate`/`not_a_bug`/`escalated` naming a live replacement: `_completion_precheck` returns a DISPOSITION verdict (`close_precheck.py:441-446`) that IS signed, but is not a completion PASS and must not read as one |
| `gate_off` | `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close` was false |
| `gate_unreadable` | the config could not be read and `gate_enabled` **failed OPEN** (`_commands/gates.py:79-87`), skipping the gate with only a stderr warning — a FAULT, and recording it as `gate_off` would launder it into a policy choice |
| `force_bypassed` | `--force` skipped the gate by operator approval |
| `local_source` | unattested local-source close (`close_precheck.py:585-586`) |
| `not_certifiable` | `certifiable is False` withholding (`close_precheck.py:589-600`) |
| `not_applicable` | `idea -> closed`: a REJECT/DROP, not a completion |

**The event records the EXPECTATION only, never the outcome.** The outcome is not knowable at
that point: the STATUS event commits BEFORE signing is attempted, which is the ordering that
causes this whole bug family. A reader derives the three states by combining the durable
expectation with the durable attestation:

* `required` + completion attestation present -> closed and signed
* `required` + attestation absent -> **closed with the signature LOST** (the state damselfly
  can only report ephemerally)
* `disposition` + attestation present -> closed and signed as a DISPOSITION, not a verified
  completion (the manifest's first line carries `DISPOSITION <class>`)
* `disposition` + attestation absent -> a disposition close whose signature was lost
* anything else -> not expected, and the value says exactly why

**How the value is computed and threaded.** It is NOT `verified_result`. That is `None` for a
`--force` close even though a signature WAS expected, and `None` for gate-off, so it conflates
the very states this ticket separates. `close_precheck` already distinguishes all six cases at
the points cited above but discards the distinction, returning only a verdict-or-`None`. So:
`_completion_precheck` returns the expectation alongside its verdict, `close_ticket` passes it
into `txn.transition_core`, and `transition_core` — which today accepts no such parameter —
gains one and writes it into the STATUS event `data` next to the present-only `close_class`
(`txn.py:287-288`), following that field's present-only precedent.

**Reduced state, not just the event.** AC2 requires a reader to work from reduced state, so the
field must be folded and declared, not merely written: `close_class` is folded by
`_fold_close_class` at BOTH `*->closed` sites in `reducer/_processors.py` (the fork-winner edge
and the plain edge), and declared in `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`. `completion_expectation`
follows that same path in the same change — an event field with no fold would leave AC2
unsatisfiable.

Damselfly's ephemeral `completion_signature.cause` is NOT the same vocabulary: it reports an
OUTCOME to the caller, where this records an EXPECTATION durably. Where they overlap
(`force_bypassed`) the spelling is deliberately shared. The field is present-only, so a reader
that does not know it degrades safely — the precedent `COMPLETION_VERDICT` already follows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `completion_expectation` is written into the close STATUS event in the SAME locked write
      as the close, taking no additional write-lock — verified by a test asserting the lock is
      acquired exactly once
- [ ] A later reader, holding no lock and reading only reduced state, separates
      closed-and-signed (`required` + attestation) from closed-with-signature-lost (`required`,
      no attestation) from closed-with-gate-off (`gate_off`) — verified by a test closing one
      ticket each way and asserting all three read back distinctly
- [ ] Each of `force_bypassed`, `local_source` and `not_certifiable` is recorded as ITSELF and
      never as `gate_off` — verified by a test per value
- [ ] `idea -> closed` records `not_applicable`, matching damselfly's rule that a REJECT/DROP
      is not a completion — verified by a test
- [ ] The expectation is computed independently of `verified_result`, so a `--force` close
      records `force_bypassed`, not gate-off — verified by a test
- [ ] The field is documented in `docs/event-schema.md` and is present-only, so a reader that
      does not know it degrades safely — verified by a test

file_impact.reason: accept and write completion_expectation on the close STATUS event in the same locked write
compute the expectation independently of verified_result and return it
fold completion_expectation at both *->closed edges, mirroring _fold_close_class
document the new present-only STATUS field
tests separating signed / signature-lost / gate-off and the other expectations
